key_insight: The paper studies how detonation-gun sprayed WC-12Co and Al2O3-13TiO2 coatings behave tribologically, and pairs experiments with machine learning to predict wear and friction.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for selecting and optimizing wear-resistant thermal spray coatings in high-friction machine components and surface-engineering applications.
method: Compare tribological performance of WC-12Co vs Al2O3-13TiO2 D-gun sprayed coatings
Use machine-learning models to predict wear and friction behavior
Leverage coating/process-property data for predictive surface engineering
evidence_signal: From the abstract, this is a journal article in Journal of Thermal Spray Technology and uses experimental coating tribology with ML-assisted prediction, but no dataset size or metrics are given in the abstract provided.
watch_item: Predictive usefulness may depend strongly on the coating process parameters and test conditions, so model transfer to other spray setups or loads may be limited.
paper_title: Tribological Performance and Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Wear and Friction in D-Gun Sprayed WC-12Co and Al2O3-13TiO2 Coatings
